anchors.name: The Book of Doors
anchors.creator: Gareth Brown
anchors.description:
If you could open a door to anywhere, where would you go?

In New York City, bookseller Cassie Andrews is living an unassuming life when she is given a gift by a favourite customer. It's a book - an unusual book, full of strange writing and mysterious drawings. And at the very front there is a handwritten message to Cassie, telling her that this is the Book of Doors, and that any door is every door .

copy.title: Comp line
copy.body: When Women Were Dragons meets Gallant. The first brings grief and transformation in an adult, literary register; the second brings a gothic house with secrets. Both are 2022 Breakout titles with fit of 0.98 and 0.96 to the touchstones.
copy.hint: The one-line "X meets Y" that opens every pitch.
copy.author: llm

copy.title: Query letter comps
copy.body: THE LANTERN ARCHIVE [word count] will appeal to readers of When Women Were Dragons and Gallant, both published in 2022, both Breakout-size in Qloo's popularity data, and both closely tied to the audience for Piranesi, The Starless Sea, The Ten Thousand Doors of January and The Book of Doors. Its grief-shaped library and hidden dead also sit near Under the Whispering Door, a 2021 Breakout title about death and what follows, and The Book Eaters, a gothic horror title about books as a hunger. Together these show recent buying in the lane, not a single phenomenon.
copy.hint: The comparables paragraph for a query letter or proposal.
copy.author: llm

copy.title: Who it's for
copy.body: The audience that loves Piranesi, The Starless Sea, The Ten Thousand Doors of January and The Book of Doors leans female and over-indexes at 30–34 (+0.20), while under-indexing among 35 and older. Its taste descriptors include metafictional, fate, time and paced, and it reads gothic and paranormal fiction as readily as speculative. Beyond books, it also favors Welcome to Night Vale and The Adventure Zone in podcasts and Mitski, Lucy Dacus and Phoebe Bridgers in music. For retail, the brands to reach it through include Epic Reads, Barnes & Noble, Strand Bookstore and Goodreads. Emerging markets include Providence, Buffalo, Hartford and Spokane. This is aggregate taste, not a forecast.
copy.hint: A short, evidence-backed paragraph about the audience.
copy.author: llm

copy.title: For fans of
copy.body: For fans of When Women Were Dragons, Gallant, Piranesi and The Book of Doors: a night-shift archivist, a library wing that rearranges itself around grief, and someone hiding the dead.
copy.hint: A one-liner for bios, store pages, press kits and posts.
copy.author: llm

copy.title: Ad hooks
copy.body:
• Loved When Women Were Dragons? Grief reshapes a whole library here, and someone is using it to hide the dead.
• For readers of Gallant: a house of secrets that is also an archive, and it moves when no one is looking.
• If Piranesi left you wanting more endless halls, this wing rearranges itself around the people who mourn.

kit.headline: Piranesi-and-The Starless Sea readers are buying When Women Were Dragons and Gallant now, and The Book of Doors shows the door-and-library lane is still moving, which is where this book sits.
kit.summary: The book sits in the library-and-doors fantasy lane, with a grief-driven, gothic mystery edge and a magical realism lean. Lead with When Women Were Dragons and Gallant: both are recent Breakout titles with the highest fit to the touchstones. Aim at readers aged 30–34, the one age band that over-indexes, and at a female-leaning audience. Drop the older planned comps in favor of titles from the last five years.
